title: Network toxicology and bioinformatics reveal potential molecular links between cadmium exposure and pancreatic cancer.
summary: Network toxicology intersected cadmium-related genes with pancreatic-cancer transcriptomics, then used machine learning to identify FN1, COL5A1, AHR, COL3A1 and TIMP1 as core candidate genes; cell-exposure assays tested proliferation and invasion.
ai_technology: Network toxicology intersected cadmium-related genes with pancreatic-cancer transcriptomics, then used machine learning
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University

evidence.tested: Independent datasets and in-vitro assays supported cadmium-associated ECM and collagen-remodeling links, while docking predicted dacomitinib binding to FN1; the study does not establish human causality.
evidence.unknown: The reviewed source does not establish prospective benefit, broad external validity, or replication beyond the reported study.
